text.title: Python Type Hints Failure Modes
text.summary: 7 antipatterns observed in real Python typing rollouts. Each has a symptom, a root cause, and a fix the validator or CI gate can enforce.

antipattern.symptom: `from __future__ import annotations` added project-wide; FastAPI body parsing or Pydantic v1 models throw `Type 'X' is not defined` at runtime; type-check passes silently.

root-cause.source: FastAPI issue tracker; Pydantic v1 docs

antipattern.root-cause: `from __future__ import annotations` stringifies all annotations at runtime. Pydantic v1 and older FastAPI body-parameter resolution use runtime type inspection and break silently when annotations are strings.
antipattern.fix: Pin Pydantic v2 + FastAPI ≥0.100 if `from __future__ import annotations` is desired, or omit the future import on files that define Pydantic v1 models / FastAPI body params. CI grep: `grep -l 'from __future__ import annotations' $(grep -rl 'BaseModel\|@app\.\(get\|post\)')`.

antipattern.symptom: Files contain `# type: ignore` with no error code; new type bugs are masked because mypy can no longer surface them; `warn_unused_ignores` cannot fire because there's no code to compare.

root-cause.source: Internal — observed in test-author subagent runs Q1 2026

antipattern.root-cause: Under pressure from a mypy gate the agent reaches for the broadest silencer first. Bare `# type: ignore` is faster to write than diagnosing the actual mismatch.
antipattern.fix: ruff rule PGH003 forbids bare `# type: ignore`. Require the coded-plus-reason form `# type: ignore[arg-type] # reason: upstream stub is wrong, see issue #123` so the ignore is auditable years later. Enforce `warn_unused_ignores = true` in mypy config so stale coded ignores fail too. Block PRs that introduce bare ignores.

antipattern.symptom: Code calls `isinstance(obj, MyProto)` where `MyProto(Protocol)` lacks `@runtime_checkable`. Runtime `TypeError: Instance and class checks can only be used with @runtime_checkable protocols`.
antipattern.root-cause: Protocol is opt-in for `isinstance` because runtime structural checks walk the MRO and signature list — too slow to enable by default. The error surfaces only at runtime, not at type-check.
antipattern.fix: Either add `@runtime_checkable` (accept the perf cost) OR replace `isinstance(x, Proto)` with structural duck-typing (`hasattr(x, 'send')`). Lint: `mypy --strict` does not catch this; add a custom grep rule.

antipattern.symptom: New code ships `def f(x: Any) -> Any: ...`. The checker reports zero errors on the module and IDE autocomplete goes dead for every caller downstream.
antipattern.root-cause: `Any` is the annotation that always satisfies the checker, so under a strict gate it is the fastest way to make the error disappear. Being valid everywhere, it silently propagates: every value derived from an `Any` is itself `Any`.
antipattern.fix: Replace with the concrete type, a `Protocol`, or `object` plus an explicit narrowing at the point of use. Enable `disallow_any_explicit` (mypy) or `reportAny` (pyright) on new modules so the shortcut fails CI rather than review.

antipattern.symptom: A public function or library export has no annotations. Consumers get no autocomplete, and `mypy --strict` fails the module with `no-untyped-def` the moment it enters the allowlist.
antipattern.root-cause: Internal helpers were typed first because they were easier, and the public surface — the one place where types are the contract — was left for later.
antipattern.fix: Type every public signature (args + return) before any internal helper; seed `strict_files` with the public-API manifest so the boundary is the first thing the gate covers.

antipattern.symptom: A per-iteration loop constructs a Pydantic model for each record; profiling shows validation dominating CPU time on a path that handles already-validated internal data.
antipattern.root-cause: "Pydantic at the boundary" was read as "Pydantic everywhere". Validation cost is per instantiation, so moving it inside a loop multiplies a one-off boundary cost by N.
antipattern.fix: Validate once at the boundary, then carry a `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)` or `TypedDict` through the loop. See `pydantic-at-io` and `typeddict-vs-pydantic` in content/01-core-rules.xml.

antipattern.symptom: Same module mixes `Optional[X]`, `X | None`, and `Union[X, None]`, and still carries `from typing import List, Optional, Union` — a deprecated-alias import that buys nothing. Ruff UP007 warnings accumulate; new contributors copy the closest example, perpetuating the mix.
antipattern.root-cause: Multiple equivalent syntaxes exist for historical reasons; without a linter, drift is the default. The single-syntax convention requires enforcement, not preference.
antipattern.fix: Enable ruff rule UP007 and run `ruff check --fix --select UP007 .` as a one-shot migration. Add the rule to pre-commit. Result: only `X | None` remains in the codebase.
